name: Aashka Hospitals Limited
summary: Aashka is a single-location Gandhinagar hospital with a prospective, unpriced expansion transaction. Its operating margin has recovered and debt has fallen, but revenue remains below pre-COVID scale and a large part of its capital is tied in legacy property/other advances. At the dated 19 October close of ₹99.90, equity value is ₹233.77 crore, about 70 times reported FY26 profit before normalization. This is a difficult turnaround/asset-recovery special situation, not a demonstrated compounder. The decisive issue is the recoverability and deployment of capital, not a hospital-sector growth slogan. BQS is 3.0 after the stewardship cap, GQS 2.45, and IAS NS. Classification: Avoid — governance, with a separate financial-reliability hold. A reconciled asset ledger, verifiable recoveries, improved recurring hospital economics and fully specified expansion terms would be needed to reopen the thesis. [S1,S4,S5,S8,S10]
identity_note: Annual and official master reconcile BSE543346 and 23.4 million shares; original listing stated 1 September 2021.

quote.kind: dated secondary close, not executable quote

score_note: BQS 3.30 raw capped3.00 for GOV 3; GQS 2.45; IAS NS with R missing and G2 hold. No ranking eligibility.

gates.reason: Historical material stewardship/documentation failures support GOV 3; current unmodified audit is contrary evidence. No intentional wrongdoing conclusion.

₹56.19 crore legacy property/other advances and ₹5.18 crore unclassified current assets, missing referenced notes and confirmation/reconciliation wording prevent a reliable full-entity valuation bridge. Historical operating figures remain usable within stated limits.
Modest hospital-only paths are conditionally funded; actual demand-debt renewal and unpriced acquisition terms remain unresolved. No observed default inferred.
Lowest-band conditional historical capacity is supported, but missing secondary rows are not verified zeros and current BSE restrictions/live execution remain unverified.

GOV.reason: Repeated material advance-deployment and documentation failures, including the historical auditor conclusions and still-large unreconciled legacy balances, support weak stewardship. Current unmodified audit, reduced debt and disclosure of the new MoU are contrary evidence. This is not an allegation of fraud.

MOAT.reason: Specialist beds and local clinical infrastructure offer access, but overlapping regional networks and sales below pre-COVID scale do not demonstrate durable pricing power. Established operations are a positive; current utilization/customer retention evidence is limited.

REV.reason: Prefer the available five-year comparable legal-entity revenue CAGR−10.77%, not the favorable three-year recovery6.70%. COVID elevated the starting base, but seven-year growth is also negative and FY26 is only 1.61%; no discretionary adjustment. Stronger second half is contrary evidence, not proof of sustained acceleration.

DUR.reason: Healthcare demand and existing beds offer accessible demand, but demonstrated scale remains weak and current utilization is unavailable. The proposed 70% acquisition has neither a verified purchase price nor funded execution bridge; no acquisition runway bonus.

CAP.reason: Persistently low operating capital returns and failed/delayed legacy deployment support the lower band. Shrinking capital makes incremental ROIC NM, so the conclusion uses multi-year operating economics and allocation outcomes, not the undefined ratio. Debt reduction is positive but not evidence of high new-project returns.

CASH.reason: Hospital cash conversion is mixed rather than mechanically disastrous: multi-year reported CFO is positive, while legacy recoveries drive much of the surplus and FY26 cash after core capex/interest is negative. Receivable days increased to 110.5. IPO advance cash classified in CFO is not counted again as a separate operating-failure penalty.

BAL.reason: Reported debt has fallen materially and modest hospital-only paths can fund themselves; current net debt/core EBITDA is around0.75x. However cash in hand, demand facilities, unknown acquisition cost and advance recoverability create stress sensitivity. Historical withdrawn D is not a current default finding.

EXEC.reason: Earlier wellness/tie-up plans were cancelled and promised refunds remain insufficiently bridged; operating revenue remains below pre-COVID levels. Debt reduction and improved recent operating margin are positives. New incorporation cancellation and a separate MoU are tracked distinctly, not treated as completed expansion.

EARN.reason: Reported EPS 1.43 and PAT growth around2.2% contrast with much lower normalized hospital profit; interest and exceptional credits materially affect reported earnings. Core EBITDA margin improved to 22.77%, a real positive, but it has not established durable owner-earnings growth.

R.reason: A full-entity investable return case is not supported while material legacy recoveries/current assets and potential acquisition terms remain unresolved. Hospital-only and recovery-grid IRRs are explicit diagnostics, not a supported base return.

D.reason: Conditionally self-financed hospital bear diagnostic loses roughly 93% of terminal share value versus dated entry. Combined demand-debt withdrawal and 20%receivable cash loss causes a 1.59 crore buffer gap. This is model stress, not observed insolvency; base liquidity remains positive.

P.reason: Approximately70x reported PAT and much higher normalized profit multiple require substantial operating improvement or asset realization. Even full face recovery in the base diagnostic remains below current price;15%hurdle algebra needs about 196 crore hospital revenue at 10xEBITDA/23%margin versus 23 crore today.

L.reason: Both observed-only and conditional missing-as-zero60-session treatments exceed20 exit sessions at 5% participation, supporting the lower band. Unknown restrictions/spread can worsen or prevent execution, not justify a higher historical-capacity grade. Lot fits the reference position; G4 remains Conditional.

BQS.cap_reason: GOV 3 stewardship override; NS remains NS. G2 also blocks investment ranking.

IAS.cap_reason: GOV 3 stewardship override; NS remains NS. G2 also blocks investment ranking.

ranking_eligibility.reason: Governance override and material G2 asset-reliability hold; numerical quality judgments retained for audit, not ranking.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Aashka Hospitals Limited, BSE SME 543346/AASHKA, ISIN INE0EAX01014. Cutoff: 20 October 2026 UTC. The annual report states listing on 1 September 2021; a later security-master date is not substituted for the original listing date. Dated secondary close ₹99.90 on 19 October; 2.34 crore actual shares; market capitalization ₹233.766 crore. Financial scope is standalone Indian GAAP Accounting Standards under Section 133. The May results auditor wording mentions Ind AS 34, whereas the issuer notes and annual presentation use AS; no unverified accounting-regime conversion is assumed. Model horizon: FY27–FY31, approximately 4.44 years to 31 March 2031; nominal equity hurdle 15%, with 12%/18% sensitivities; analytical cost-of-capital range 11–14%; liquidity reference ₹5 lakh, not a recommended position. [S1,S6,S7,S10,S11]

G1 Integrity: Conditional. Substantiated historical stewardship failures support GOV 3, but no current fraud or diversion finding is made. G2 Reliability: Hold — unresolved. The issue is economically material: ₹56.19 crore property/other advances plus ₹5.18 crore unclassified current assets, missing referenced notes, and current confirmation/reconciliation wording prevent an investable full-entity asset/return bridge. This is not merely a typographical discrepancy or a blanket rejection of audited revenue. G3 Funding: Conditional. Reduced debt and modest hospital-only cases are manageable; an unpriced acquisition and refinancing stress remain unresolved, not an observed default. G4 Tradability: Conditional. Dated eligible series/lot and trading observations support a lowest-band liquidity estimate, not restriction clearance or guaranteed execution. Historical operating inputs and bounded quality judgments have Medium confidence; legacy recoverability/full valuation confidence is Low; overall investment confidence Low and forecast uncertainty High. [S1,S8,S11]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors: GOV 3, MOAT 4, REV 1, DUR 4, CAP 2, CASH 5, BAL 5, EXEC 3, EARN 3. BQS contributions 0.60+0.80+0.12+0.40+0.24+0.50+0.40+0.24=3.30 raw, capped at 3.00 because GOV≤3 on documented stewardship evidence. GQS contributions 0.40+0.80+0.45+0.30+0.50=2.45; persistent weak capital allocation activates the 5.0 cap but it is nonbinding. Coverage is 100% for both, with factor-specific Medium confidence on these bounded judgments. The recovery uncertainty does not make the historical weak returns disappear; nor is an assumed write-off used to manufacture them. [E2–E10]

IAS: Q 3.00, R NS, D 2, P 2, L 1. Known weighted contribution 1.45; coverage 65%; uncapped missing-data arithmetic bound 1.80–4.95, not a score. The governance ceiling would limit a subsequently supportable IAS to 3, but cannot replace NS. G2 independently excludes investment and numerical quality rankings where asset reliability is central. All ranking flags are false. A one-point change in GOV and CAP changes raw BQS by 0.32 and raw GQS by 0.15; the governance cap changes only if the stewardship evidence changes. No midpoint or renormalization is used. [E5,E6,E7,E11,E12]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The issuer describes 150 beds including 65 ICU beds, cardiac and other operating theatres, diagnostic and pharmacy services at Gandhinagar. This is capital- and clinician-intensive inpatient/outpatient care, not a fee-light platform. FY25 disclosed inpatient revenue ₹17.64 crore, outpatient ₹1.25 crore, pharmacy ₹3.52 crore and canteen ₹0.24 crore. FY26 revenue is ₹23.01 crore, but the missing revenue note prevents claiming a verified current mix. Patients and institutional payers generate revenue; the detailed payer concentration and current collection terms are not sufficiently disclosed to assume cash-at-treatment economics. Closing receivables ₹6.97 crore amount to 110.5 sales-proxy days. [S1,S2]

Annual capacity is a management disclosure, not independent operational certification. The website's older ICU count differs, so the dated annual 65 is used. IPO occupancy 65.9%/65.2% in FY20/FY21 is historical only. Current occupancy, ARPOB, case mix and clinical outcomes were not established; there is no invented bed-utilization forecast. The proposed Rhythm restructuring/acquisition is outside the historical perimeter and reference revenue until completion and terms are verified. [S1,S6,S8]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Clinical capabilities, installed infrastructure and local referral relationships can create switching and trust advantages, but this record does not establish differentiated pricing power or durable patient-share gains. Apollo's Ahmedabad facility is on the Ahmedabad–Gandhinagar corridor; Shalby has SG Highway and other Ahmedabad capacity; Sterling lists Gurukul and Sindhubhavan locations. These are primary-source commercial competitors, not matched financial valuation peers. Their network presence makes a generic regional-demand thesis insufficient. No inference about comparative clinical quality is made. [S14,S15,S16]

The contrary evidence to a strong moat is operating scale below FY2019 despite the installed bed base, and low operating returns on capital. Positive evidence is continuing specialist operations and the FY26 operating-margin recovery. Doctor retention, payer negotiations, equipment replacement, service quality and local competition are failure modes. No patient/customer concentration percentage or precise market share is invented from missing disclosure. MOAT 4 reflects demonstrated weakness versus positive infrastructure, not a penalty merely for small size. [S1,S6]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Revenue in ₹ crore: FY19 27.6666; FY20 27.2282; FY21 40.6888; FY22 39.7336; FY23 18.9447; FY24 22.8739; FY25 22.6468; FY26 23.0103. Five-year FY21–26 CAGR is−10.77%; three-year FY23–26 is+6.70%; seven-year FY19–26 is−2.60%. A ten-year comparable series was not recovered. Five years is selected before scoring because the same legal-entity revenue scope is available. Pandemic demand distorts the high base, but the pre-pandemic comparison also contracts; choosing only the favorable recovery window would overstate the evidence. [S1–S6]

Annual additions FY22–26 are−₹0.9552, −₹20.7889, +₹3.9292, −₹0.2271 and+₹0.3635 crore. FY26 growth is 1.61%, not a high-growth trajectory. H1FY26 revenue ₹10.4437 crore was down about 15.5% versus the derived ₹12.3643 crore H1FY25; H2FY26₹12.5666 crore was up 22.2% against ₹10.2825 crore. This recovery is meaningful contrary evidence, but two opposite halves do not establish sustained acceleration. H2 PAT ₹2.5589 crore includes ₹1.9621 crore other income, so reported profit acceleration cannot stand in for revenue growth. No H1FY27 results ending September 2026 are assumed available. Organic price, volume and mix contributions cannot be separated reliably. [S7]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Demand for hospital care and existing capacity provide a possible runway, but current utilization and revenue-per-bed evidence are insufficient for a fully underwritten bottom-up expansion case. The model therefore tests modest hospital paths, not a target forecast: base 5% annual revenue growth and 23% EBITDA margin; bull 10/10/10/8/6% growth with 24–26% margins; bear−5/−5/0/0/0% and 16–18% margins. No Rhythm revenue is included. Base FY31 revenue is ₹29.37 crore, versus about ₹35.06 crore in the bull. Growth is matched with cash capex, operating working capital and interest rather than treated as free. [S1,S8]

Opening operating WC is actually reconciled ₹5.1596 crore, not a forecast percentage imposed backward. Incremental requirements are 30% of positive sales additions in base/bull and 50% in bear, with no automatic release on falling sales. Base capex begins ₹2.5 crore and rises 5% annually; bull ₹3.0/3.3/3.6/3.9/4.2 crore; bear ₹2.5 crore annually. These are maintenance/expansion sensitivities, not issuer commitments; annual plus/minus ₹1 crore is tested. Economic depreciation approximates 7.15% of opening fixed assets, and tax is 26% of positive operating PBT without loss-credit monetization. [S1]

Reported capital has not earned the analytical 11–14% hurdle: FY26 normalized average-total-capital ROIC is 1.55%, and even removing all legacy property/other advances from closing capital leaves low single-digit returns. Capital shrinkage makes incremental ROIC NM, not excellent. Persistent allocation weakness drives CAP 2 and the nonbinding GQS cap; mixed hospital cash conversion is scored separately. The unpriced 70% acquisition is a contingent strategic option with potential financing demands, not verified value creation. [S1,S2,S4,S8]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
FY22's qualified auditor report described ₹28.7042 crore MD advance without an agreement provided, ₹28.615 crore hospital tie-up advances with absent progress/interest support, and ₹8.1712 crore other advances without supporting documents/confirmation. FY23's qualified report discussed ₹35.965 crore advances,₹3.058 crore interest charged, and an auditor-stated ₹2.1349 crore unconfirmed-interest effect on assets/loss, plus an unexecuted ₹28.6675 crore land deed and incomplete IPO debt-repayment use. These are attributed historical audit findings, not our finding of intentional wrongdoing. The FY26 statutory and secretarial opinions are unmodified, a material positive that is not omitted. The earlier auditor change followed term expiry, not a verified protest resignation. [S4,S5,S1]

Promises versus delivery: the FY23 response cancelled wellness/tie-up plans and contemplated refunds; by March 2026 aggregate property/other advances still total ₹56.19 crore. The MD property-advance related-party row falls to nil from ₹25.63 crore, but aggregate property advances remain ₹22.33 crore. That does not prove an equivalent cash refund; counterparty and reclassification bridges are needed. Debt did fall to ₹8.23 crore, a delivered improvement. August 7's MoU provides for 70% of a restructured Rhythm business at a future transaction valuation. August 27 explicitly abandons proposed Aashka–Rhythm subsidiary incorporation, not explicitly the separate MoU; neither completion nor wholesale cancellation is asserted. [S1,S4,S8,S9]

FY26 remuneration ₹1.44 crore is about 43% of reported PAT, unchanged from FY25 and above FY24 nil; this is an allocation consideration, not automatic abuse. The reported negative ₹0.591 crore remuneration balance is not treated as a positive liability or a separate recoverable asset without its ledger. Annual promoter holdings are 61.28%; a different secondary 61.34% series is not silently substituted, and current pledges are unverified. September 24 shareholders approved accounts, CMD reappointment, borrowing and investment powers; those approvals are not sanctioned or unused bank finance. October 3's response to a BSE price query attributes movement to market conditions. A price query is not proof of manipulation. [S1,S2,S18,S17]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The attached structured history retains eight revenue/profit years and six cash-flow/balance-sheet years with original/comparative scope labels. FY24/25/26 revenue is ₹22.8739/22.6468/23.0103 crore; PAT ₹2.3578/3.2661/3.3389; CFO ₹7.1773/9.1899/7.7932; cash capex ₹0.6735/1.3791/2.8211. Reported CFO-minus-capex proxies are ₹6.5038/7.8108/4.9722. Three-year cumulative CFO/PAT is 24.1605/8.9628=2.6957x, but CFO contains legacy noncurrent-asset releases. Five-year CFO/PAT is−37.4663/8.7589=−4.2775x, dominated by FY22₹66.3402 crore noncurrent-asset cash absorption classified in CFO. Neither ratio alone describes hospital cash quality. FY23 original CFO ₹4.0924 crore becomes ₹1.0067 crore after ₹3.0857 crore interest-income reclassification; no second subtraction is made. [S1–S5]

FY26 PBT ₹3.9561 crore includes other income ₹2.2691 and exceptional credit ₹0.5957; core PBT is ₹1.0913. Excluding both, PAT ranges ₹0.4741 crore if actual tax is unchanged to ₹0.8075 crore at a normalized 26% rate. Cash-flow financial interest ₹1.9280 leaves ₹0.3411 crore residual other income that may include recurring rent/miscellaneous income: retaining it gives core EBIT ₹2.6129 rather than ₹2.2718 crore. The exceptional credit's nature was not established and is not invented. FY25 disclosed lab rent is a reason not to call all other income nonrecurring. Core EBITDA ₹5.2402 crore and 22.77% margin improved, but reported PAT overstates the conservative hospital-earnings boundary. [S1,S2,S7]

FY26 CFO ₹7.7932 less net noncurrent-asset release ₹4.4261 leaves ₹3.3671; less capex ₹2.8211 and financing-classified interest ₹1.1805 gives−₹0.6345 before interest income. Property advances fell ₹6.3397 while other advances rose ₹1.9635; the net release must not be described as all cash recovery from the MD. Receivables rose ₹2.2516 crore to ₹6.9681 despite 1.61% sales growth; closing sales-proxy days increased from about 76 to 110.5. FY26 other current assets ₹5.1845 lack the referenced detail in this copy. FY25's tax/supplier/prepayment composition is not imposed on FY26, and unverified MAT credits are not monetized. [S1,S2]

Opening claims map: inventory ₹0.3891, receivables ₹6.9681, staff advances ₹0.0527 and operating deposits ₹1.2133 less operating trade payables ₹1.5125, other current liabilities ₹0.8973 and recurring short provisions ₹1.0537 yield operating WC ₹5.1596. Other current liabilities include statutory dues ₹0.7988 and customer advances ₹0.0985; short provisions include employee ₹0.3180 and expense/other ₹0.7357. They are retained as recurring opening/forecast stocks, not arbitrarily liquidated: prior statutory dues were ₹0.7092 crore, employee provisions ₹0.3036 crore and expense/other provisions ₹1.0790 crore. Their recurring categories and comparable prior balances support a normal-cycle reference, not a claim that overdue sums can remain unpaid indefinitely. Separate accelerated-settlement stresses remove all short provisions, and then both provisions plus statutory dues, from opening WC and pay them once without assuming replacement credit. No distinct opening income-tax payable is disclosed; cash flow reports full MAT expense paid. All ₹5.1845 unclassified current assets are excluded from both WC and reference recovery, avoiding tax-credit double counting. [S1]

Capital creditors ₹0.0252 are excluded from WC and paid once. Current debt maturities ₹0.4251 are already within total debt ₹8.2348 and are not added again. Noncurrent gratuity ₹0.3461 and returnable deposits ₹0.5040 remain terminal claims; future employee costs are expensed in cash. Reported cash ₹4.3229 comprises ₹2.5501 cash in hand,₹0.0561 current bank balance and ₹1.7168 debit cash-credit balance, the latter not extra borrowing. Cash-in-hand availability has a separate stress. Annual note 39 reports nil contingent liabilities/commitments, not independent legal clearance. Note 40's no-CWIP wording conflicts with ₹2.0033 crore CWIP and its ageing schedule; current Tally audit-trail nonoperation is also disclosed. Alongside missing notes 14–25 and confirmation wording, these justify specific caution, not an assertion that all reported assets are fictitious. [S1]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹99.90, equity value ₹233.766 crore is about 70.0x reported PAT and 2.26x book equity. After reported net debt, EV is approximately ₹237.68 crore or 45.4x conservative core EBITDA. These multiples do not prove fair value: book contains material uncertain advances and PAT contains non-hospital/exceptional contributions. No hospital-peer multiple is borrowed without accounting for scale, mix and returns. The 6/10/14x bear/base/bull exit EBITDA assumptions are declared analyst sensitivities, not observed peer medians. [S1,S10]

Hospital-only annual reference paths are conditionally self-financed with existing demand debt renewed, no new bank rescue and a ₹1 crore buffer. Later principal ₹0.50 crore/year is an analyst amortization sensitivity, not a verified contractual schedule. FY31 diagnostic terminal prices are ₹7.12/29.62/55.48 in bear/base/bull, with friction-adjusted diagnostic IRRs−45.33%/−24.63%/−13.19%. Every funded_investment_IRR remains null: these are diagnostic operating/recovery bounds, not investable price targets while G2 and acquisition scope are unresolved. No dividends, new shares or speculative acquired earnings are assumed. Entry and exit friction are 2% each, not guaranteed execution costs. [S1,S8,S10]

Legacy property ₹22.3275 and other advances ₹33.8618 are outside operating WC and have zero reference recovery/terminal addition. Separate 0/50/100% recovery grids pay equal installments in FY28–30, without forecasting interest or double-counting terminal assets. Base 50% recovery of both gives ₹41.63; full recovery gives ₹53.64; full recovery also of the ₹5.1845 current-asset bucket gives ₹55.85. These are face-value sensitivities, not probabilities or claims of realizable value. Base margin−3 percentage points gives ₹24.59; capex+₹1 crore/year ₹27.56; no cash-in-hand availability ₹28.53; all short provisions settled once ₹29.17. [S1]

Reverse expectation: at 10x EBITDA and 23% margin, the 12/15/18% equity hurdles require approximately ₹174.19/195.98/219.82 crore FY31 revenue under the fixed-share algebra, versus ₹23.01 crore now. Funding, capacity and utilization for that scale are not established. Exit-only margin 18/23/28% by multiple 6/10/14 is supplied separately from linked annual margin/capex paths. A conditional entry range is not offered because asset recovery and transaction terms are not sufficiently underwritten. [S1,S8,S10]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest positive counterargument is that a low-debt hospital can keep generating cash while legacy advances are recovered at face and existing capacity fills. The model gives that argument explicit recovery sensitivities rather than presuming zero is the only possible outcome. Nevertheless, even full base recovery of all three identified buckets is below the dated price under stated operating/multiple assumptions. A much faster operating ramp, higher terminal pricing or additional valuable acquisition would be needed, none established here. [S1,S8]

A credible loss path combines weak demand, replacement capex, slow collection and refinancing withdrawal. The hospital bear reference is conditionally funded but loses about 93% of terminal share value versus entry. With the ₹2.1323 crore demand facility withdrawn and 20% of receivables lost in cash, peak buffer need is ₹1.59 crore. Any retained terminal equity is an UNFUNDED mechanical sensitivity, not a financeable target. Hypothetical ₹5/10/20 crore acquisition cash costs, with no invented income, create base buffer gaps ₹0.82/5.82/15.82 crore; these are not quoted deal prices. Actual unknown terms could differ materially. [S1,S8]

The historical March 2025 CRISIL D/issuer-not-cooperating rating was withdrawn after company request and bank NOC; the agency stated it lacked forward-looking information. Its ₹33.15 crore facility figure is historical, not current debt. It supports monitoring information access, not a current-default claim. Thesis-break variables are further unreconciled advance deployment, inability to collect operating receivables, new unfunded commitments or erosion of hospital earnings before fixed costs and debt service. [S13,S1]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Five times current equity value is ₹1,168.83 crore; ten times is ₹2,337.66 crore. Even at 25x owner PAT and 10% owner margin, these require ₹46.75/93.51 crore PAT and ₹467.53/935.06 crore revenue, roughly 20/41 times current sales. This is fixed-share algebra, not a forecast. Existing 150-bed capacity without verified utilization/ARPOB, historical low returns, and unspecified acquisition finance do not establish such a route. Legacy recoveries can release capital but are finite assets, not a recurring compounding engine; funding through new equity would raise the business-scale requirement per existing share. A5×/10× claim is unsupported. [S1,S8,S10]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Reconcile ₹22.3275 crore property and ₹33.8618 crore other advances by counterparty, ageing, legal terms, cash recoveries and current confirmations; movements must tie to bank cash, not just an RPT reclassification.
2. Obtain the missing FY26 notes 14–25 and a bridge for ₹5.1845 crore current assets, including tax-credit usability, plus the negative remuneration balance. Do not net unverified credits against liabilities.
3. Track recurring core EBITDA ₹5.2402 crore, core PBT ₹1.0913 crore and the nature of ₹0.5957 crore exceptional credit. Two comparable periods of operating improvement matter more than other-income gains.
4. Track receivable ₹6.9681 crore/110.5 sales-proxy days. Further deterioration above 120 days without an evidenced payer explanation is an analytical warning, not a covenant breach.
5. Publish current occupancy, ARPOB, payer mix, clinician retention and commissioned capacity. Historical 65% occupancy is not a current baseline.
6. Reconcile demand facility ₹2.1323 crore, actual amortization, cash-in-hand ₹2.5501 crore and unrestricted bank cash. A negative cash bridge or verified nonpayment would require a new funding-gate assessment.
7. Obtain Rhythm MoU termination/completion status, exact consideration, share issuance, liabilities assumed and funding. Do not equate cancelled incorporation with cancelled acquisition.
8. Confirm current promoter/pledge data, audit-trail remediation and the CWIP wording/ledger correction. Shareholder borrowing approval alone is not financing.
9. Recheck actual-position liquidity, current BSE restrictions and lot at any contemplated trade. Current lot 1000 costs ₹99,900; five lots ₹499,500 before costs. Historical capacity does not assure exit.
Review upon the next signed half-year results, material recovery/acquisition filing or exchange restriction change; no automatic monitoring service is implied. [S1,S7,S8,S9,S10,S11]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Avoid — governance under the explicit GOV≤3 framework rule; separate Hold — unresolved financial reliability. BQS 3.0 and GQS 2.45 do not qualify as a compounder. IAS remains NS, so no fabricated matrix cell or return-ranked recommendation is assigned. All ranking eligibility flags are false because the material asset/reliability questions are central. This is a completed evidence-bounded research review, not a declaration that missing issuer evidence has been resolved. [S1,S4,S5]

A lower quote alone does not fix stewardship, confirmation or acquisition-scope gaps. Reconsider only after an auditable recovery/use-of-funds bridge, adequate current disclosures and demonstrably improving recurring operating returns; then rerun the funded per-share model and current implementation test. For any existing holder, actual position size, costs, taxes and alternatives must be assessed separately. The ₹5 lakh capacity test is not a suitable-allocation recommendation or an instruction to trade. [S1,S8,S10]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The source ledger distinguishes signed issuer documents retrieved through public mirrors, issuer-hosted annual/IPO documents, historical rating analysis, official exchange master/calendar evidence, primary competitor pages and dated secondary OHLCV. All were accessed 20 October 2026. Local text extraction was checked against original annual layout for the missing-note issue; the May condensed results do not supply the missing detail. Older annual accounting reclassifications are preserved rather than blended into a false homogeneous series. The later signed October 3 clarification and September 25 AGM report were read; neither establishes an acquisition closing or bank availability. [S1–S19]

Remaining material uncertainties are advance recoverability/counterparties, current-asset and exceptional-income composition, actual demand-debt terms and later amortization, current promoter encumbrances, current BSE restrictions, occupancy/ARPOB and the proposed 70% transaction's final scope/funding. No independent legal/court clearance or current bank-rating replacement was established. These limits are attached to the affected factor or gate, not converted into fabricated low scores. Model growth, margins, tax, capex, working-capital increments, recovery timing, exit multiples and friction are assumptions explicitly separable from reported facts. There is no assertion of fraud, diversion, market manipulation or current default. [S1,S8,S13,S17]

limitations: This is a hospital-only capital and recovery diagnostic, not a complete current investable entity valuation. The separate Rhythm MoU has no verified final price/funding/closing.

All unconfirmed property/other advances and unclassified current assets are segregated from operating WC and receive no reference recovery or terminal addition; recovery grids are bounds, not estimated probabilities. No accrued advance interest is forecast.

Ordinary statutory, employee and expense liabilities have consistent opening and forecast closing-stock treatment. Separate reclassification stress removes short provisions from opening WC and pays them once; it does not credit any tax asset. No specific opening current-income-tax payable is disclosed separately.

Current-asset note 17 is absent in the examined FY26 annual copy; all5.1844792 crore is excluded from cash recovery and operating WC in the reference. Prior-year tax-credit composition is not imposed on current balances.

Current debt maturities are included in debt, capital creditors paid once, noncurrent gratuity and returnable deposits retained as terminal claims. New annual employee benefits are included in cash operating expenses.

Reported cash includes 2.5500621 crore cash in hand; availability is a sensitivity, not independently physically verified. No new bank rescue in reference; existing demand debt is assumed renewed except withdrawal stress.

Capex is not proven maintenance:2.5 crore base start versus 2.8211last actual, plus/minus 1 crore annual stress. Economic DA7.15% of opening operating fixed assets approximates FY26, not a detailed replacement schedule.
Forecast growth, margins and 6/10/14x exit EBITDA are analyst sensitivities, not peer-derived fair multiples. All returns include2% entry and exit friction, not guaranteed execution costs.

No dividends or share dilution; this does not imply a potential acquisition can be financed without new equity. Buffer1 crore is analytical. Tax26%, no loss tax credit/refund and no immediate shield for current draws.
